title: Young Problem Solvers — Foundation

lessons.title: Number Detectives: Place Value
lessons.question: How does the position of a digit change its value?
learningObjectives: Represent five-digit amounts using ten-thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens and ones.
Compare and order amounts without guessing from the first digit alone.
Explain a comparison using place-value language.

lessons.title: Estimate, Calculate, Check
lessons.question: How can an estimate help us catch mistakes?
learningObjectives: Round whole-number prices to the nearest 100 or 1,000.
Estimate a sum, then calculate it exactly.
Assess whether an answer is reasonable and check it using another strategy.

lessons.title: Budgets and Priorities
lessons.question: What must we pay for before we choose extras?
learningObjectives: Distinguish total budget, reserved money, required costs and optional purchases.
Compute an accurate subtotal using multiplication and addition.
Decide how much remains available without spending reserved money.

lessons.title: Choices, Trade-offs and New Information
lessons.question: Which affordable plan best meets a goal?
learningObjectives: Compare alternative shopping plans against an explicit budget constraint.
Explain why an affordable plan may still be less suitable than another.
Revise a plan when a price, reserve or requirement changes.

lessons.title: Equal Groups and Whole Packets
lessons.question: What does a remainder mean when buying whole packets?
learningObjectives: Model equal groups using repeated addition and multiplication.
Divide a quantity by packet size and interpret the remainder.
Round UP to the next whole packet when partial packets cannot be purchased.

lessons.title: Comparing Value for Money
lessons.question: What is the cheapest feasible way to supply enough cups?
learningObjectives: Calculate the total number of packets needed for a target quantity.
Compare total purchase costs, not just price per packet.
Use evidence to recommend a feasible purchasing plan.

publicationNotice: Draft for expert review. No evidence of validated learning gains or school accreditation.

weeks.title: Number detectives
objectives: Read, compare and partition whole numbers in everyday examples.
Round to useful place values and estimate sums before calculating.
Check a calculation using a second strategy and explain a discrepancy.
weeks.drivingQuestion: How do we know if a numerical answer makes sense?

weeks.title: Budget choices
objectives: Add and subtract UGX amounts accurately and keep track of a reserve.
Distinguish required purchases from optional ones.
Compare affordable plans using calculations and a clear explanation.
weeks.drivingQuestion: How can a limited budget guide our decisions?

weeks.title: Groups, rates and sharing
objectives: Model equal groups with multiplication and related division.
Interpret a unit price and compare two offers of the same quantity.
Explain remainders correctly in a real-life situation.
weeks.drivingQuestion: When should we multiply, divide or estimate?

weeks.title: Measure before deciding
objectives: Choose suitable units for length and capacity.
Estimate and then measure with appropriate tools.
Record measurements with units and calculate simple totals/differences.

weeks.title: Collect and display data
objectives: Formulate a neutral, answerable question.
Collect and organize small anonymous datasets using tallies.
Construct/read a simple bar chart with titles and labelled axes.
weeks.drivingQuestion: How can evidence help us notice patterns?

weeks.title: Claims and evidence
objectives: Read values, totals and differences from a graph or table.
Separate what a dataset shows from what it does not show.
Use a calculation and evidence to support a short written claim.
weeks.drivingQuestion: When is a claim stronger than a guess?

weeks.title: Patterns and rules
objectives: Extend arithmetic and shape patterns from an explicit rule.
Describe a rule in words, tables or arrows.
Test a proposed rule with a new input and find counterexamples.
weeks.drivingQuestion: Can we describe a rule precisely enough to predict?

weeks.title: Logic and instructions
objectives: Order actions as a finite sequence and identify missing steps.
Follow constraints when planning a route or arrangement.
Debug instructions and communicate the correction clearly.

weeks.title: Build, test, improve
objectives: Specify a clear success criterion before a trial.
Run at least three fair trials and record observations.
Use test results to make and justify one improvement.
weeks.drivingQuestion: How do we know whether a design really works?

weeks.title: Fractions in decisions
objectives: Represent common fractions as equal parts of a whole.
Calculate unit fractions and familiar fractions of whole-number quantities.
Explain a stock allocation using fractions and counts.
weeks.drivingQuestion: How can parts of a whole affect a plan?

weeks.title: Mini-enterprise decisions
objectives: Calculate total cost and revenue from quantities and unit amounts.
Distinguish revenue from surplus and explain why both matter.
Revise a plan when a constraint or demand estimate changes.
weeks.drivingQuestion: How do we compare income, cost and surplus?

weeks.title: Final challenge and reflection
objectives: Complete an independent, unfamiliar multi-step problem using appropriate strategies.
Present one project decision supported by calculations or measurements.
Identify personal growth, a remaining gap, and an actionable next goal.
weeks.drivingQuestion: What can I now solve independently and explain to others?
